blocks.p: A spreadsheet assumes every client pays on the due date. Real clients don't.

blocks.b: Swipe to see what that costs.

blocks.p: $188,900 of bills land in a single week: the staff bonus, payroll and insurance.
The spreadsheet says cash is fine, because it counts a late client's payment as already paid.

blocks.b: Swipe to see what it misses.

blocks.p: It reads three years of invoices and payments and learns how each client really pays. One hotel client pays about 42 days late.
Week six really closes at $19,934, $10,066 under the minimum. Move the staff bonus back two weeks and it becomes $102,934.

blocks.b: You see the gap over a month early, and test the fix first.

blocks.p: Weeks 12 and 13 still dip below the minimum, and now there's time to plan for them.

blocks.b: You're in control of your cash, with no need to stress.

blocks.p: Our next post is an 85-second video: a wholesale bakery, a late-paying client and the fix.
